name: Marquardt
desc: Family-owned German maker of steering-wheel systems, control panels, vehicle access and battery-management electronics and appliance switches, founded in 1925.

name: Alo Yoga
desc: Los Angeles-founded premium yoga and athleisure apparel brand with flagship stores and wellness clubs expanding across Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

name: Tricon Energy
desc: Houston-based global distributor and trader of basic chemicals, polymers, fuels and raw materials and fertilizers, serving partners in 120+ countries.

name: Gebr. Heinemann
desc: Hamburg family-owned travel-retail and duty-free distributor running about 500 shops, 340 at airports, and supplying customers in over 100 countries.

name: Qualtrics
desc: Experience-management software company providing customer, employee and market research survey and analytics platforms to enterprises worldwide.

name: Golden Goose
desc: Italian luxury sneaker and ready-to-wear brand known for hand-distressed trainers, majority-owned by HSG since late 2025.

name: Grupo Luckia
desc: Galician gaming group operating betting shops, casinos, slot venues and online betting in Spain, Latin America, Portugal, Croatia and Cameroon.

name: Remondis
desc: Germany's largest waste management, recycling and water services company, operating in more than 30 countries as part of the family-owned Rethmann group.

name: Topgolf
desc: Operator of tech-enabled golf entertainment venues in the US and abroad, majority-owned by Leonard Green & Partners since November 2025.

name: flydubai
desc: Dubai government-owned low-cost airline flying about 130 routes from Dubai International with a Boeing 737 MAX fleet.

name: Tod's
desc: Italian luxury shoe and leather-goods group owning Tod's, Hogan, Fay and Roger Vivier, taken private in 2024 with L Catterton.

name: San Carlo
desc: Italy's leading potato-chip maker, producing San Carlo crisps and salty snacks at four Italian plants and sponsoring MotoGP and football.

name: Schauinsland-Reisen
desc: Family-run German tour operator from Duisburg selling package holidays to about two million customers, with stakes in two airlines.

name: Eurofarma
desc: Brazilian-owned pharmaceutical company with over 430 products, plants in thirteen countries and operations across all of Latin America, Africa and the USA.

name: Solenis
desc: Platinum Equity-owned specialty-chemical maker supplying water treatment, process and functional chemistries and monitoring systems to industrial customers.

name: alltours
desc: German package tour operator founded by Willi Verhuven, carrying 2.3 million holidaymakers a year and owning 29 allsun hotels.

name: Wieland Gruppe
desc: Ulm-based maker of copper and copper-alloy rolled, extruded and engineered products and thermal solutions, with about 60 companies in 40 countries.

name: Reinhausen
desc: Family-majority German maker of on-load tap-changers, transformer monitoring, power-quality and grid-regulation equipment for utilities and transformer manufacturers.

name: Cvent
desc: Event-management software company based near Washington, D.C., serving corporate event planners, taken private by Blackstone in 2023.

name: Boots
desc: Health and beauty retailer and pharmacy chain with about 3,900 stores worldwide, separated from Walgreens Boots Alliance after the Sycamore take-private.

name: Banka Creditas
desc: Czech commercial bank of the privately owned Creditas Group, serving retail and business clients and owning MeDirect in Malta and Belgium.

name: Epic Games
desc: Developer and publisher of Fortnite, maker of Unreal Engine and operator of the Epic Games Store on PC and mobile.

name: The Ardonagh Group
desc: Private equity-backed international insurance broking platform from the UK, expanding through acquisitions in Ireland, Australia, Spain and New Zealand.

name: Disaronno Group
desc: Reina family-owned Italian spirits group behind Disaronno amaretto, renamed from ILLVA Saronno, which bought Averna from Campari in 2026.

name: uvex
desc: German maker of ski and cycling helmets, goggles and occupational safety products, majority-owned by Warburg Pincus since 2025.

name: Daher
desc: Family-controlled French aircraft maker (TBM, Kodiak) and aerostructures, industrial services and logistics supplier operating in 17 countries.

name: ATI Global
desc: Australian founder-led group owning legal and property-technology businesses InfoTrack, Smokeball, LawConnect, Sympli, Groundsure and CreditorWatch.

name: Mirabaud
desc: Family-owned Geneva private bank run by six partners, offering wealth management, asset management and brokerage from offices in Europe, Canada, Asia and the Gulf.

name: Prozis
desc: Founder-owned Portuguese sports nutrition and fitness products maker selling online across Europe, with ten factories in Portugal.

name: Farmers Insurance
desc: US insurer group selling auto, home, life and small-business insurance through exclusive agents; management company owned by Zurich Insurance Group.

name: Duvenbeck
desc: German owner-managed logistics group serving the automotive, consumer goods, plastics and agricultural-vehicle industries from 37 sites in eight countries.

name: Teneo
desc: New York CEO advisory firm combining strategic communications, restructuring, risk and investor relations, majority owned by CVC, with 1,600+ staff in 40+ offices.

name: Ferrero
desc: Family-owned confectionery and packaged-food group behind Nutella, Kinder, Ferrero Rocher and Tic Tac, now also Kellogg's cereals in North America.

name: Figure AI
desc: Venture-backed developer of general-purpose humanoid robots and the Helix vision-language-action model for factory, logistics and home work.

name: Redwood Materials
desc: US battery recycling and battery-materials company founded by J. B. Straubel, recovering lithium, nickel and cobalt and building second-life energy storage.

name: Van Mossel
desc: Dutch automotive dealer group with more than 600 branches in seven European countries, plus body repair and car leasing businesses.

name: I Squared Capital
desc: Miami infrastructure investor owning energy, transport, digital and social infrastructure companies across the Americas, Europe and Asia.

name: Moon Active
desc: Private Tel Aviv mobile games developer behind Coin Master, which reached USD 6bn lifetime revenue by August 2024.

name: Heathrow Airport
desc: Owner and operator of London Heathrow, Europe's busiest hub airport, held by Ardian, QIA, PIF, GIC and other funds.

name: Sedgwick
desc: Carlyle-controlled claims management and risk administration provider with 33,000+ colleagues in 80 countries, valued at USD 13.2bn in 2024.
